title: Eating out with friends
goal: Suggest food with 'I feel like…', order for a group at a street cart or café, say 'too spicy', 'not enough salt' and 'a little', and sort out the bill: my treat, or split it.
intro:
Eating out in Odisha usually means street food with friends: **ଗୁପଚୁପ** (Odisha's pani puri) at a cart, Cuttack's **ଦହିବରା ଆଳୁଦମ** (lentil dumplings in yoghurt with spicy potato curry), chaat in the evening, and **ଛେନାପୋଡ଼** or **ରସଗୋଲା** to finish. Cafés and restaurants are part of it too, especially in Bhubaneswar.

This unit teaches the most Odia way to say what you fancy, **ମୋର … ଖାଇବାକୁ ମନ ହେଉଛି** 'I feel like eating…', and the words for adjusting your order: **ଅତି** 'too', **ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ** 'enough', **ଅଳ୍ପ / ଟିକେ** 'a little'. Then the bill: **ଆଜି ମୋ ଟ୍ରିଟ୍!** 'my treat today!' or **ବିଲ୍ ଭାଗ କରିବା** 'let's split it'.

vocab.note: ମୋର + -ବାକୁ + ମନ ହେଉଛି: ମୋର ଚା ପିଇବାକୁ ମନ ହେଉଛି 'I feel like a tea'. Lit. 'my mind is (turning) to…'.

vocab.en: gupchup (pani puri: crisp puffs with spicy tamarind water)
vocab.note: Spoken without the inner vowels: gupchup. Golgappa in Delhi, phuchka in Kolkata.
Lentil dumplings in thin spiced yoghurt, with spicy potato curry (ଆଳୁଦମ) and yellow-pea ଘୁଗୁନି, topped with onion and sev.
ଠେଲାରେ ଖାଇବା 'to eat at a street cart'.
ଅର୍ଡର ଦେବା also works. Online: ଅର୍ଡର କରିଦେଲି 'I've placed the order'.
Street food is ordered by the plate: ଦୁଇ ପ୍ଲେଟ୍ ଚାଟ୍ 'two plates of chaat'. Number + ପ୍ଲେଟ୍, no ଟା.
To call him: ଭାଇ! or ଶୁଣନ୍ତୁ! Never snap your fingers.
ପାଣି ମାଗ 'ask for water'. To ask a *question* is ପଚାରିବା.
ଅତି ରାଗ 'way too spicy'. ବହୁତ ବେଶି means the same in speech.
ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ହେଲା 'that's enough'; ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ନାହିଁ 'not enough'.
ରାଗ ଅଳ୍ପ 'not too spicy', ଅଳ୍ପ ଚିନି 'a little sugar'.
Green chilli: କଞ୍ଚା ଲଙ୍କା. Spicy-hot is ରାଗ.
Many families avoid onion and garlic on fast days and festivals; ପିଆଜ ବିନା is a common request.
Adjective: ସୁଆଦିଆ "tasty".
Lit. 'burnt cheese': fresh chhena, sugar and cardamom baked until caramelised.
Odisha's rasagola (with a GI tag, 'Odisha Rasagola') is softer and creamier than the Bengali one, and Odias will tell you it came first.
ବାଣ୍ଟି ଖାଇବା 'to share (food)'.
ଜଣ ପିଛା 'per person', ପ୍ଲେଟ୍ ପିଛା 'per plate'.
ଭାଗ କରିବା 'to divide, split'; ମୋ ଭାଗ 'my share'.
ଆଜି ମୋ ଟ୍ରିଟ୍ 'it's my treat today'; ଟ୍ରିଟ୍ ଦେବା 'to treat (people)'.

grammar.title: Too, enough, a little: ଅତି, ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ, ଅଳ୍ପ, ଟିକେ
grammar.body:
**A lot / very**: ବହୁତ, and colloquially ଭାରି: ଭାରି ସୁଆଦିଆ 'really tasty'.

**Too (much)**: **ଅତି** + adjective: ଅତି ରାଗ 'way too spicy', ଅତି ଦାମୀ 'too expensive'. In everyday speech **ବେଶି** or **ବହୁତ ବେଶି** does the same job, and context tells you it's 'too': ଚିନି ବେଶି ହୋଇଗଲା 'there's too much sugar' (lit. 'the sugar became more').

**Enough**: **ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ**: ଦୁଇ ପ୍ଲେଟ୍ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ 'two plates is enough'; ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ହେଲା 'that's plenty'. **Not enough**: ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ନାହିଁ, or simply କମ ଅଛି 'it's short': ଲୁଣ କମ ଅଛି 'it needs more salt'.

**A little**: **ଟିକେ** (ଟିକିଏ) before an adjective or noun: ଟିକେ ରାଗ 'a bit spicy', ଟିକେ ପାଣି 'a little water'. **ଅଳ୍ପ** means 'only a little, not much', perfect for requests: ରାଗ ଅଳ୍ପ ଦେବେ 'go easy on the chilli'. **A bit more / less**: ଟିକେ ଅଧିକ / ଟିକେ କମ.

**So … that**: **ଏତେ … ଯେ …**: ଏତେ ରାଗ ଯେ ମୋ ଆଖିରୁ ପାଣି ବାହାରିଲା 'so spicy that my eyes watered'.

**Trap**: ଅଳ୍ପ and ଟିକେ are not the same as ଅତି. 'A bit spicy' (ଟିକେ ରାଗ) is a compliment at a street cart; 'too spicy' (ଅତି ରାଗ) is a complaint.

grammar.title: I feel like…: ମୋର … -ବାକୁ ମନ ହେଉଛି
grammar.body:
The everyday way to say what you fancy uses **ମନ** 'mind, heart'. The person is in the **genitive** (ମୋର 'my', ତୋର, ତୁମର, ତାଙ୍କର), the activity is in the **-ବାକୁ** form, and **ମନ ହେଉଛି** follows: literally 'my mind is (turning) to eating…'.

ମୋର ଗୁପଚୁପ **ଖାଇବାକୁ ମନ ହେଉଛି** — I feel like gupchup.
ତୋର କ'ଣ ଖାଇବାକୁ ମନ ହେଉଛି? — What do you feel like eating?
ଆଜି ମୋର ବାହାରକୁ ଯିବାକୁ **ମନ ହେଉନି** — I don't feel like going out today.
ଖରାଦିନେ ପଖାଳ ଖାଇବାକୁ **ମନ ହୁଏ** — In summer you (always) feel like pakhala.
ମୋର ଆଇସକ୍ରିମ୍ ଖାଇବାକୁ **ମନ ହେଉଥିଲା** — I was craving an ice cream.

Shorter: **ମନ ନାହିଁ** 'not in the mood': ମୋର ଯିବାକୁ ମନ ନାହିଁ. You'll also hear the dative (ମୋତେ … ମନ ହେଉଛି), but ମୋର is the most common.

Compare: **ଭୋକ ଲାଗୁଛି** 'I'm hungry' (Unit 5); **ଇଚ୍ଛା** 'wish' (Unit 17) is a little more formal: ମୋର ଯିବାକୁ ଇଚ୍ଛା ଅଛି 'I'd like to go'.

**Trap**: don't say ମୁଁ … ମନ ହେଉଛି. The subject of ହେଉଛି is ମନ, so 'I' must be ମୋର.

examples.native: ମୋର କିଛି ମିଠା ଖାଇବାକୁ ମନ ହେଉଛି।

culture:
Street food is social in Odisha: friends stand round a **ଠେଲା** while the vendor hands out gupchup one at a time, each person saying ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ 'one more' until they're done (ବାସ୍). Cuttack is famous for **dahibara aludum** for breakfast and in the evening; Bhubaneswar for evening chaat, egg rolls and the cafés of Saheed Nagar and Patia. Sweets are a point of pride: **ଛେନାପୋଡ଼** (from Nayagarh), Salepur's **ରସଗୋଲା**, and the long-running rasagola rivalry with Bengal.

Paying is a little contest. Someone says ଆଜି ମୋ ଟ୍ରିଟ୍! and the others protest, and it's polite to protest once or twice. Whoever has had good news (a job, a birthday, passing an exam) is expected to give a **ପାର୍ଟି** or **ଟ୍ରିଟ୍**. Among students and young colleagues, splitting the bill by UPI (ଜଣ ପିଛା…) is completely normal. At sit-down places call the waiter with **ଭାଇ!** or **ଶୁଣନ୍ତୁ!**; tipping is small and optional. Remember that many Odias eat no onion, garlic or meat on certain days (Mondays, Kartika month, festival days), so ask before ordering for the group.

tip.title: ମୋର … -ବାକୁ ମନ ହେଉଛି
tip.body:
- 'I feel like…' = **ମୋର** + verb-**ବାକୁ** + **ମନ ହେଉଛି**: ମୋର ଚାଟ୍ ଖାଇବାକୁ ମନ ହେଉଛି.
- Not in the mood: **ମନ ହେଉନି** / **ମନ ନାହିଁ**. Always: **ମନ ହୁଏ**.
- The person is ମୋର / ତୋର / ତାଙ୍କର, never ମୁଁ.

lessons.title: Ordering for the group

tip.title: Ordering
tip.body:
- Get attention: **ଭାଇ!** or **ଶୁଣନ୍ତୁ!**
- Number + **ପ୍ଲେଟ୍** + dish: ଦୁଇ ପ୍ଲେଟ୍ ଚାଟ୍. For drinks and pieces use -ଟା: ଚାରିଟା କଫି.
- **ଆମ ପାଇଁ** 'for us', **ମୋ ପାଇଁ** 'for me'; ask for things with **ମାଗିବା**.

new: ଆମ ପାଇଁ ଚାରି ପ୍ଲେଟ୍ ଦହିବରା ଆଳୁଦମ।

sentences.native: ଆଉ ଦୁଇଟା ଗୁପଚୁପ ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ, ଭାରି ସୁଆଦିଆ!
sentences.roman: au duiṭa gupchup diôntu, bhari suadia!
sentences.en: Two more gupchup please, they're delicious!

sentences.native: ଆପଣମାନେ କ'ଣ ଅର୍ଡର କରିବେ?
sentences.roman: apôṇômane kôṇô ôrḍôr kôribe?

sentences.roman: e kapherô kôphi sôhôrôre sôbuṭharu bhôlô.
sentences.en: This café's coffee is the best in town.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ମେନୁ ଦେଖି ଅର୍ଡର କରିବି।
sentences.roman: muṃ menu dekhi ôrḍôr kôribi.
sentences.en: I'll look at the menu and then order.

tip.title: Too, enough, a little
tip.body:
- **Too**: **ଅତି** + adjective (ଅତି ରାଗ); in speech also ବହୁତ ବେଶି.
- **Enough**: **ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ**; not enough: ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ନାହିଁ / କମ ଅଛି.
- **A little**: **ଟିକେ**; 'only a little': **ଅଳ୍ପ** (ରାଗ ଅଳ୍ପ ଦେବେ).
- **So … that**: ଏତେ … ଯେ …
tip.pattern: ଅତି + adj · ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ (ନାହିଁ) · ଅଳ୍ପ / ଟିକେ + noun

sentences.native: ତରକାରୀରେ ଅତି ଲଙ୍କା, ମୁଁ ଖାଇପାରୁନି।
sentences.roman: tôrôkarire ôti lôṅka, muṃ khaiparuni.
sentences.en: There's way too much chilli in the curry, I can't eat it.

sentences.native: ଲୁଣ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ନାହିଁ, ଟିକେ ଲୁଣ ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: luṇô jôthesṭô nahiṃ, ṭike luṇô diôntu.
sentences.en: There's not enough salt, could I have a little?

sentences.native: ମୋ ପାଇଁ ମସଲା ଅଳ୍ପ ଦେବେ।
sentences.roman: mo paiṃ môsôla ôḷpô debe.
sentences.en: Go easy on the spices for me, please.

sentences.native: ତରକାରୀ ଏତେ ରାଗ ଥିଲା ଯେ ମୋ ଆଖିରୁ ପାଣି ବାହାରିଲା!
sentences.roman: tôrôkari ete ragô thila je mo akhiru paṇi baharila!
sentences.en: The curry was so spicy my eyes watered!

sentences.native: ପିଆଜ ବିନା ଦେବେ, ମୁଁ ପିଆଜ ଖାଏ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: piajô bina debe, muṃ piajô khae nahiṃ.
sentences.en: No onion, please, I don't eat onion.

sentences.native: ଦୁଇ ପ୍ଲେଟ୍ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ହେବ।
sentences.roman: dui pleṭ jôthesṭô hebô.
sentences.en: Two plates will be enough.

sentences.native: ଚାରେ ଚିନି ଟିକେ ବେଶି ହୋଇଗଲା।
sentences.roman: chare chini ṭike besi hoigôla.
sentences.en: There's a bit too much sugar in the tea.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଲଙ୍କା ଖାଇପାରେ, ହେଲେ ଏତେ ନୁହେଁ!
sentences.roman: muṃ lôṅka khaipare, hele ete nuheṃ!
sentences.en: I can handle chilli, but not this much!

sentences.native: ଗୁପଚୁପ ପାଣିରେ ଟିକେ ଅଧିକ ଖଟା ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: gupchup paṇire ṭike ôdhikô khôṭa diôntu.
sentences.en: A bit more sour in the gupchup water, please.

sentences.native: ଛେନାପୋଡ଼ର ସ୍ୱାଦ ପୂରା ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ!
sentences.roman: chhenapoṛôrô swadô pura ôdbhutô!
sentences.en: Chhena poda tastes amazing!

sentences.native: ଏ ଚାଟ୍ ଟିକେ ଫିକା, ଲୁଣ ଦରକାର।
sentences.roman: e chaṭ ṭike phika, luṇô dôrôkarô.
sentences.en: This chaat is a bit bland, it needs salt.

sentences.native: ଏଠି ଖାଇବା ଭାରି ତେଲିଆ।
sentences.roman: eṭhi khaiba bhari telia.
sentences.en: The food here is really oily.

sentences.native: ଚାଲ, ଗୋଟିଏ ଛେନାପୋଡ଼ ବାଣ୍ଟି ଖାଇବା।
sentences.roman: chalô, goṭie chhenapoṛô baṇṭi khaiba.
sentences.en: Let's share a chhena poda.

sentences.native: ଆମ ରସଗୋଲା ସବୁଠାରୁ ଭଲ!
sentences.roman: amô rôsôgola sôbuṭharu bhôlô!
sentences.en: Our rasagola is the best!

sentences.native: ଆଉ ଖାଇପାରିବି ନାହିଁ, ପେଟ ପୂରିଗଲା।
sentences.roman: au khaiparibi nahiṃ, peṭô purigôla.
sentences.en: I can't eat any more, I'm full.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ମୋ ରସଗୋଲା କାହା ସହ ବାଣ୍ଟିବି ନାହିଁ!
sentences.roman: muṃ mo rôsôgola kaha sôhô baṇṭibi nahiṃ!

sentences.native: ତେଲିଆ ଖାଇବା ଖାଇ ମୋ ପେଟ ଖରାପ ହୋଇଗଲା।
sentences.roman: telia khaiba khai mo peṭô khôrapô hoigôla.
sentences.en: I ate greasy food and got an upset stomach.

sentences.native: ବୋଉ ରାନ୍ଧିଲେ ସ୍ୱାଦ ଅଧିକ ଭଲ ଲାଗେ।
sentences.roman: bou randhile swadô ôdhikô bhôlô lage.
sentences.en: Food tastes better when Mum cooks it.

lessons.title: My treat, or shall we split it?

tip.title: Paying with friends
tip.body:
- Offer: **ଆଜି ମୋ ଟ୍ରିଟ୍!** Expect a protest or two: ନା ନା!
- Split: **ବିଲ୍ ଭାଗ କରିବା**; each: **ଜଣ ପିଛା** + amount.
- Good news (a job, a birthday) means you pay: ଟ୍ରିଟ୍ ତୋର!

sentences.native: ନା ନା, ଆଜି ମୋ ଟ୍ରିଟ୍, ମୋର ଚାକିରି ମିଳିଲା!
sentences.roman: na na, aji mo ṭriṭ, morô chakiri miḷila!
sentences.en: No no, it's my treat today, I got the job!

sentences.native: ବିଲ୍ ଚାରି ଭାଗ କରିବା।
sentences.roman: bil chari bhagô kôriba.
sentences.en: Let's split the bill four ways.

sentences.native: ଜଣ ପିଛା ଶହେ ଟଙ୍କା ପଡ଼ିଲା।
sentences.roman: jôṇô pichha sôhe ṭôṅka pôṛila.
sentences.en: It came to a hundred each.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ୟୁପିଆଇ କରିଦେଉଛି, ତୁମେମାନେ ମୋତେ ପଠାଇଦେବ।
sentences.roman: muṃ yupiai kôrideuchhi, tumemane mote pôṭhaidebô.
sentences.en: I'll pay by UPI, you lot send me your share.

sentences.native: ଏଇ ଦୁଇଟା ରୁଟି ପ୍ୟାକ୍ କରିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: ei duiṭa ruṭi pyak kôridiôntu.
sentences.en: Could you pack up these two rotis?

sentences.native: ଗତ ଥର ତୁ ଦେଇଥିଲୁ, ଆଜି ମୁଁ ଦେବି।
sentences.roman: gôtô thôrô tu deithilu, aji muṃ debi.
sentences.en: You paid last time, I'll pay today.

sentences.native: ଜନ୍ମଦିନ ତ ତୋର, ଟ୍ରିଟ୍ ବି ତୋର!
sentences.roman: jônmôdinô tô torô, ṭriṭ bi torô!
sentences.en: It's your birthday, so the treat's on you!

sentences.native: ଦୁଇଟା ଛେନାପୋଡ଼ ପ୍ୟାକ୍ କରିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ, ଘର ପାଇଁ।
sentences.roman: duiṭa chhenapoṛô pyak kôridiôntu, ghôrô paiṃ.
sentences.en: Pack two chhena podas to take home, please.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଭାଗର ପଇସା ମୁଁ ଦେଇଦେଲି।
sentences.roman: mo bhagôrô pôisa muṃ deideli.
sentences.en: I've paid my share.
